hypotheses.theory: A shared pool can help cash-poor agents deliver profitable funded services when the customer locks payment until acceptance and paid inputs cannot be obtained free or prepaid. Borrower profit comes from useful work sold to an independent buyer; lender fee must be explicit and smaller than verified surplus.
alternative_explanations: Buyers can pay input advances directly and eliminate credit demand.
Providers are operator-funded and do not need loans.
Observed agent commerce is shared-controller/testing/subsidized activity rather than independent profitable demand.

predictions.observable: A funded independent order, real paid input invoices, accepted useful work, loan repayment from buyer proceeds and positive provider net cash margin.
predictions.disconfirming_observation: Only team-funded jobs/repayment grants; no cash gap or net surplus after all costs.

predictions.observable: A repeat provider self-finances once earnings exceed its working-capital gap.
predictions.disconfirming_observation: Repeated borrowing required only to generate reputation or subsidized loan counts.

hypotheses.confidence_scope: Conditional structural analogy; no success probability or measured commercial loan profitability.
